rv.q: The Morbs is–in these post-COVID days–a very unsettling and engaging work that finds some big laughs even at moments that shouldn't be all that funny.
Unfortunately, there is little tension until almost the final scene which. This undermines the play as a thriller, though the relationship between the women is well defined.
The vibrant performances as Trish, Wendy, and Tatum convey both the personalities the friends knew in college and the women they have become.
Those minor missteps do not detract from the overall strength of the play.

cn.t: Critics praise Jen Diamond's play as powerful ensemble theatre, with dynamic performances elevating this story of female friendship during a pandemic outbreak, though the premise proves more effective than its execution.
